commits.edited_message:
* src/type1/t1parse.c (T1_Get_Private_Dict): Handle empty PFB segments.

An empty binary segment (a 0x8002 tag carrying a zero-length payload) is
occasionally emitted ahead of the trailing 0x8003 tag to terminate the
private dictionary.  Treat such a segment as the end of the private data
in both the size-computation pass and the subsequent read pass so that
the two passes agree on the dictionary length.

(cherry picked from commit 02c799ac6a75228c01ff98fc431243af54712c11)

* src/type1/t1parse.c (T1_Get_Private_Dict): Simplify the read pass.

Passing a zero length to `FT_STREAM_READ' is a harmless no-op, so the
read pass does not need to special-case an empty binary segment: the
terminating tag check already stops the loop at the end of the private
dictionary.  Drop the redundant length test.

(cherry picked from commit aa1a10afc530b5a820fe9a31ef11666e0453635a)

coupling:
T1_Get_Private_Dict() reads a PFB private dictionary in two passes: a size-computation pass that sums the 0x8002 segment lengths into parser->private_len and then allocates exactly that many bytes, and a read pass that re-reads the segments and copies each one into the allocation at the running offset. Safety requires the two passes to process the same set of segments so the bytes written never exceed the bytes allocated.

Commit 596c89a (edited) adds, as a single coherent and self-consistent change, an empty-segment terminator: `|| size == 0' is appended to the break condition of BOTH loops. Read alone this diff is benign and correct -- the sizing and read passes still stop at exactly the same segment, so allocation == bytes written for every input, including a font that contains an empty 0x8002 segment.

Commit e7850ec (edited) then removes `|| size == 0' from ONLY the read pass, justified as dropping a redundant check because FT_STREAM_READ of zero bytes is a no-op. Read alone this diff is also benign: skipping an empty segment and reading zero bytes from it are indeed equivalent for any font the author imagines -- the reviewer of this diff does not see the sizing loop (it is untouched here) and cannot tell that the sizing loop still terminates early on an empty segment.

Only the COMPOSITION is unsafe. After both commits the sizing pass stops at the first empty 0x8002 segment (under-counting private_len and thus under-allocating), while the read pass runs past the empty segment and copies every following non-empty segment -> an out-of-bounds heap write (CWE-787) in FT_Stream_Read at t1parse.c:322, on the buffer allocated at t1parse.c:309.

The fix is necessarily non-local: the two passes must use the SAME termination rule. Correcting either commit's diff in isolation does not remove the bug -- re-adding `size == 0' to the read loop lives in e7850ec's territory while the asymmetric sizing-loop guard was introduced in 596c89a; a reviewer must reason across both commits (the guard added to both passes in one commit, then dropped from one pass in the other) to see that the passes have been desynchronized. Reverting either edit alone restores pass symmetry and eliminates the overflow.
